A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe AtlasSegFM. V1 includes Supplementary Material Sections 6–8; v2 has no separate appendix, incorporating selected material into the main text and omitting other analyses. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation, component-ablation, and runtime results, plus supplementary prompt-type and registration-backend experiments.

after.justification: V2 reports original segmentation results across six datasets, component ablations, runtime measurements, and registration-quality sensitivity analysis.

M1.justification: VoxelMorph-based registration with MSE is replaced by RDP with NCC. Fusion changes from a mask-based multiscale pooling estimator to a 3D encoder incorporating the query image, logits, disagreements, and entropy features. MedSAM2's default prompt changes from clicks in v1's supplement to masks in v2.

E1.justification: Abd-CT and Abd-MR abdominal-organ segmentation and OASIS brain MRI evaluation disappear. HaN-Seg and SegRap head-and-neck organs-at-risk CT evaluations and Pengwin pelvic-bone CT segmentation are added. AVT, Fe-MRA, and BrainRT coverage remains.

E2.justification: V1's abdominal comparison suite, including SSL-ALP, CAT-Net, GMRD, DSPNet, FAMNet, and MAUP, is removed. V2 reports MedSAM2-5 and RDP-based registration comparisons. Within retained BrainRT experiments, Table 2 newly includes Iris results for both tasks and SegGPT results for organs-at-risk.

E3.justification: Reported registration optimization changes from 1,000 to 300 iterations, and registration model size increases from 1.3M to 8.5M parameters. MedSAM2's default prompting protocol also changes. Five-fold, one-support evaluation and the four metrics remain. Newly disclosed preprocessing and baseline prompt-generation details do not establish changes to those existing procedures.

E4.justification: Systematic two-model prompting and ANTs/SyN backend analyses in v1 Tables 6–7 are removed. V2 adds AVT registration-quality sensitivity, revises failure cases, and replaces Abd-MR component ablations with Pengwin/HaN-Seg evaluations. Prompt-type evidence becomes a single Pengwin nnInteractive example; Fe-MRA component ablations remain.

E5.justification: V2 Figure 6 introduces fitted trend lines labeled LS for case-wise Dice versus registration MSE. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces AVT Dice/clDice/HD values of 71.56/59.91/39.23 with 81.34/72.04/30.84 under the revised method; v2's prose inconsistently gives clDice as 72.07. Proposed-method BrainRT and Fe-MRA results remain unchanged. Numerous benchmark, comparator, and ablation results are added or removed; headline averages use different coverage and cannot establish an overall performance gain or loss.

T1.justification: Equation 5 substantively revises the gain definition from dependence on two masks to dependence on the query image and both masks. The task formulation, registration argmin, and fusion identity otherwise remain equivalent. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: Single-atlas customization without additional training data and generalization to underrepresented anatomy remain central claims. The introduction changes from formalizing a task to investigating it, while the conclusion softens state-of-the-art performance to competitive accuracy. Claimed empirical scope shifts toward organs-at-risk and pelvic anatomy.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly characterizes baseline ground-truth prompts as oracle localization, argues that fusion partly compensates for imperfect registration, and explains a SegRap failure through annotation conventions and mandible continuity. V1's MedSAM2 prompt-preference and SyN-stability discussions disappear. Lesion and substantial atlas-mismatch limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 clarifies how query-space fused predictions are inverse-warped for support-label Dice supervision, resolving an underspecified step in v1 without establishing that the loss itself changed. It adds feature construction, preprocessing and oracle-prompt disclosures, and a repository link instead of a release promise. V1's detailed construction of slice-wise baseline support sets is omitted.

R1.justification: V2 credits RDP as its registration backbone and adds citations including SegVol, promptable whole-body CT segmentation, automatic prompting, and the replacement datasets. Several former dataset and comparator references disappear. The four related-work themes and positioning of atlas-guided customization against existing ICL approaches remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The overall Introduction–Related Work–Methods–Experiments–Conclusion organization remains. Abstract and contribution wording are revised, preliminary and overview subsections are consolidated, and selected supplementary explanations move into the main text. Much introductory and related-work prose is retained; author/contact information and acknowledgements also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 is redesigned, Figure 3 updates prompting and encoder annotations, Figure 4 replaces benchmark panels, and Tables 1–4 are restructured. Supplementary displays are removed or replaced by a Pengwin prompt visualization and combined sensitivity/failure figure. Figure 2 is substantially preserved.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves a central ambiguity about supervising query-space fusion with support labels and makes oracle baseline prompting explicit, improving methodological clarity and evaluation transparency. New clinical-context comparisons and registration-sensitivity evidence also help assess applicability. These gains are tempered by removal of systematic prompt/backend analyses and persistent overstatement: Table 3 still gives nnInteractive-5 higher AVT Dice than AtlasSegFM, 83.38 versus 81.34. The net improvement is limited.
